lyo_001: You can recognise it by its bark peeling into patches of grey, green and cream, a pale patchwork that only develops with age. It stands on the arboretum perimeter path in Parc de la Tete d'Or.
lyo_002: You can recognise it by its ridged, hollowed trunk over the lower two metres, about 3.70 metres round. It stands in the arboretum of Parc de la Tete d'Or.
lyo_003: You can recognise it by its deeply fluted, buttressed trunk, 5.45 metres round and over 30 metres tall, among the largest in the arboretum. It stands near the lake in Parc de la Tete d'Or.
lyo_004: You can recognise it by its enormous trunk carrying multiple large branches, standing out even among the park's other mature trees. It stands at the centre of Parc de la Garde.
lyo_009: You can recognise them by the mix of magnolia, cedar and horse chestnut across the garden's lawns, with a view over the Saone and Fourviere. They stand in the Jardin des Chartreux.
lyo_010: You can recognise it by its clean, even yellow autumn colour and a trunk about 3.20 metres round, 26 metres tall. It stands in the arboretum of Parc de la Tete d'Or.
lyo_011: You can recognise it by being a full-grown oak on an ordinary residential street, where plane and lime are the usual planting. It stands at Rue Viret and Rue Francis de Pressense, Villeurbanne.
lyo_012: You can recognise it by being a young, unmarked chestnut at the centre of a small square, no plaque beyond its own planting. It stands in Place Marc-Aron, rue Moncey.
lyo_013: You can recognise it by standing alone at the centre of a square barely bigger than a tennis court, where four small streets meet. It stands in Place Antoine-Rivoire.
